claim: Bourglinster Castle operates as a dining and events venue (two restaurants — La Distillerie and Brasserie Côté Cour — plus salons for weddings/conferences) rather than a ticketed museum, with no public tours advertised.
quote: Available Activities: Dining Options: The castle operates two restaurants... The website makes no mention of public castle tours, museum exhibitions, or general cultural events open to the public.

claim: Bourglinster Castle is ~17 km east of Luxembourg City, was restored after the State acquired it in 1968, and since 1982 hosts exhibitions, concerts and the Friends of Bourglinster Chamber Music Festival.
quote: Bourglinster Castle is located in the village of Bourglinster in central Luxembourg some 17 km (11 mi) to the east of Luxembourg City... After it was acquired by the Luxembourg State in 1968, the buildings were fully restored and, in 1982, opened for exhibitions, concerts, meetings and receptions.

claim: Larochette Castle is open daily 10:00–18:00 (last admission 17:00) from 15 March to 15 November 2026; adults €7, students/seniors €5, children 6–17 €4, under-6 free; LuxembourgPass and Kulturpass accepted.
quote: Every day from 10:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. with last admission at 5:00 p.m. The castle operates from March 15 through November 15, 2026. Adults: €7.00, Students (18-26) and seniors (65+): €5.00, Children (6-17): €4.00

claim: Hollenfels Castle interior is closed for renovation; only the rose garden in front and a path with steep steps to the base of the rock are publicly accessible, and the on-site youth hostel is also temporarily closed for reconstruction.
quote: Due to renovation work, the castle cannot currently be visited from the inside. However, the rose garden in front of the castle is open to the public... The youth hostel Hollenfels is temporarily closed as reconstruction works are underway.

claim: The Valley of the Seven Castles follows the Eisch valley from its confluence with the Alzette upstream to Steinfort; the seven castles are Mersch, Schoenfels, Hollenfels, the old and new Ansembourg, Septfontaines and Koerich, drivable in about an hour or hikeable on a 37-km footpath.
quote: The seven castles are: Mersch, Schoenfels, Hollenfels, the old and new castles of Ansembourg, Septfontaines and Koerich... The entire route can be traversed in about an hour by car... There is also a 37-kilometre footpath.

claim: Useldange Castle ruins host a UNESCO-sponsored discovery trail with 16 tactile and audio stations in English, French, German and Luxembourgish, plus a touchable crypt model and two permanent exhibitions on castle history and medieval daily life.
quote: The castle is unique for its UNESCO-sponsored discovery trail for partially-sighted visitors, weaving around the castle and up into the restored castle tower with a series of 16 tactile and audio experiences.

claim: Pettingen Castle ruin, ~4 km north of Mersch, is a 30-metre-square moated stronghold with four round corner towers, freely accessible 24/7 at no charge; damaged by French cannon in 1684 and state-owned since 1947.
quote: Pettingen Castle is located in the village of Pettingen some 4 km north of Mersch in central Luxembourg. This nice castle ruin is freely accessible, and entrance is free. The castle ruin is open 24/7 so you can visit it anytime you want.

claim: Mersch Castle is a Renaissance structure at Place Saint Michel now used as the commune's town hall, with public access limited to the inner courtyard; the square also features the baroque 1707 tower of the former St-Michel parish church, now a tourist info point.
quote: The building now serves as the town hall and administrative center for the local commune... You can visit the inner courtyard. The square in front of the castle has a 1707 baroque style tower of the former St. Michel church.

claim: Sanem Castle near Esch-sur-Alzette is a 16th-century rebuild (completed 1557, reconstructed around a rectangular courtyard ~1567) that has stood vacant since 2016 after stints as a children's home (Kannerschlass) and refurbishment.
quote: Today's building was completed in 1557 after the medieval castle had been partly destroyed. In about 1567, Frédéric de Hagen-Fleckenstein reconstructed the castle, placing the new buildings around a large rectangular courtyard... As of January 2025, Sanem castle has been vacant since 2016.

claim: Septfontaines Castle (Burg Simmern) in the Eisch valley burned down in 1779 and is privately owned and not visitable inside, but the ruins and rose garden in front are freely accessible year-round.
quote: The castle fell prey to a devastating fire in 1779 and burned down... Today the castle is privately owned and cannot be visited. However, the rose garden in front of the castle is open to the public. Additionally, the castle is freely accessible all year round.

claim: The National Museum of Military History in Diekirch presents WWII and the Battle of the Bulge through ~50 life-size dioramas and tens of thousands of artefacts; open daily 10:00–18:00 May–September and 14:00–18:00 October–April with €6 adult admission.
quote: Using life-size dioramas, the military museum in Diekirch shows realistic scenes from the lives of soldiers in wartime and reconstructs the battles in the surrounding area, with 50 unique dioramas, tens of thousands of exhibits.

claim: Vianden Castle lies ~47 km (about 44–50 min) by road from Luxembourg City, placing it well outside a 30 km radius from Moutfort even after accounting for Moutfort's ~10 km offset south-east of the capital.
quote: Vianden is a 47 kilometres (29 miles) drive from Luxembourg City... the fastest way to drive from Luxembourg to Vianden Castle takes 44 minutes.

claim: Moutfort sits in the Contern commune south-east of Luxembourg City, reachable from the capital in roughly 10–20 minutes by car, which sets the practical centre for a 30 km radius covering the Guttland castles cluster.
quote: Luxembourg City can be reached from Contern in less than 20 minutes... The commune of Contern is reachable by car in 10 minutes from the city of Luxembourg.
